newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates steady.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was left unchanged at a fixed rate of three percent.

The Bundesbank council's decision came after the government said on Thursday that German unemployment worsened again in February but the rise in jobless slowed, prompting analysts to predict the worst of the jobs crisis may be over.
But the jobless level, which rose a mere 5,000 to a seasonally adjusted 4.316 million in February, remains at the highest levels since the Great Depression of the 1930s.

Economists said the report would not prompt the Bundesbank to cut rates and said they see no chance of a rate cut any time soon, in part because the real interest rate level is very low and the country's monetary policy was on an expansive course.

In addition, a rise in consumer prices in the first two months of 1997 to just under two percent has done away with enthusiasm for a further rate easing in the current cycle and has prompted some talk of an interest rate increase in 1997.
